response: The implementation of the 80-hour workweek for surgical residents in New England has had mixed results. While it has improved resident well-being and reduced fatigue-related errors, some studies suggest that it may have negatively impacted the quality and quantity of surgical training. Residents may have less time for operative experience, patient care, and educational activities, potentially affecting their overall surgical competence. However, many programs in New England have adapted to the 80-hour workweek by implementing more efficient scheduling, increasing faculty supervision, and emphasizing hands-on training, which may have mitigated some of the negative effects. Overall, the impact of the 80-hour workweek on surgical resident education in New England is complex and may vary depending on the specific program and institution.
